terms.definition: A globally distributed system of servers that caches and delivers content to users from locations geographically close to them, reducing latency.
terms.example: CloudFront caches your website in 600+ edge locations so a user in Australia gets content from Sydney instead of Mumbai.

terms.definition: AWS's CDN service that distributes content to users worldwide through edge locations, reducing latency and offloading traffic from the origin server.
terms.example: A company hosts files in S3 (Mumbai) but uses CloudFront to serve them from edge locations near every user globally.

terms.definition: A geographically distributed mini data center where CloudFront caches content. Separate from AWS Regions and Availability Zones.
terms.example: London, Sydney, Tokyo, São Paulo each have CloudFront edge locations that cache website files for local users.

terms.definition: In CloudFront, the original source of your content — the server or service CloudFront fetches files from when they are not cached. Common origins include S3 buckets and Application Load Balancers.
terms.example: An S3 bucket in Mumbai is the origin. CloudFront fetches files from it and caches them at edge locations worldwide.

terms.definition: A CloudFront configuration that defines how content from an origin is delivered to users, including origin settings, caching behavior, security, and domain names.
terms.example: You create one distribution per website, specifying the S3 origin, default root object (index.html), and OAC.

terms.definition: When a requested file is already stored in a CloudFront edge location and is served directly without contacting the origin. Results in very fast delivery.
terms.example: User in Sydney requests index.html. CloudFront Sydney already has a cached copy — serves it in milliseconds without calling S3.

terms.definition: When a requested file is NOT in a CloudFront edge location. CloudFront must fetch it from the origin, cache it, and then serve it to the user.
terms.example: First user to request a file from a Sydney edge location causes a cache miss — CloudFront fetches from S3 Mumbai, caches locally.

terms.definition: The duration a cached object stays in a CloudFront edge location before it is considered stale. Default is 24 hours (86,400 seconds).
terms.example: Set TTL to 3600 (1 hour) for HTML files so changes appear within an hour, but 86400 (24 hours) for images that rarely change.

terms.definition: A CloudFront operation that removes one or more objects from all edge location caches before their TTL expires, forcing CloudFront to re-fetch from the origin.
terms.example: After deploying a new version of index.html, you create an invalidation for /index.html so users see the new version immediately.

terms.definition: A CloudFront feature that allows only a specific CloudFront distribution to access a private S3 bucket. The S3 bucket policy uses the distribution's ARN to grant access.
terms.example: S3 bucket has no public access. OAC policy allows only distribution E2QWRUH to read from it — direct S3 URLs return 403.

terms.definition: The older method (now legacy) for restricting S3 access to CloudFront. Replaced by OAC which supports more features including SSE-KMS and all S3 regions.
terms.example: Old setups used OAI. New setups should use OAC — same concept, but OAC supports more S3 capabilities.

terms.definition: AWS's authoritative DNS (Domain Name System) web service. Translates domain names like www.myshop.com into IP addresses. Named after DNS port 53.
terms.example: User types www.myshop.com. Route 53 returns the CloudFront distribution's IP so the browser connects to the nearest edge location.

terms.definition: The internet's address book — translates human-readable domain names (e.g., google.com) into machine-readable IP addresses (e.g., 142.250.80.46).
terms.example: Without DNS, you would need to type 142.250.80.46 instead of google.com in your browser.

terms.definition: A Route 53 container that holds DNS records for a domain and its subdomains. Public hosted zones route traffic on the internet; private hosted zones route within a VPC.
terms.example: Create a hosted zone for myshop.com, then add A, CNAME, and MX records inside it to control where domain traffic goes.

terms.definition: An AWS Route 53-specific record type that maps a domain name directly to an AWS resource (like CloudFront, ELB, or S3). Works at the apex domain and queries are free for AWS targets.
terms.example: Create an Alias A record for myshop.com pointing to a CloudFront distribution — works at the root domain, unlike CNAME.

terms.definition: A standard DNS record type that maps one domain name to another. Cannot be used at the apex (root) domain per DNS standards. Queries are charged in Route 53.
terms.example: CNAME for www.myshop.com pointing to d1234abcdef.cloudfront.net — valid for subdomains, but not for the bare myshop.com apex.

terms.definition: A Software Development Kit provided by AWS that allows developers to interact with AWS services programmatically using various programming languages (Python, Java, Node.js, etc.).
terms.example: A developer uses the Python SDK (Boto3) to write code that automatically uploads processed files to S3 after a job completes.

terms.definition: The official AWS SDK for Python. Allows Python developers to create, configure, and manage AWS services through Python code using client or resource interfaces.
terms.example: import boto3; ec2 = boto3.resource('ec2'); instance = ec2.create_instances(...) — launches an EC2 instance from Python.

terms.definition: A pre-configured template that contains the operating system, configuration, and software for launching an EC2 instance. AMI IDs are region-specific.
terms.example: AMI ami-0c55b159cbfafe1f5 is Ubuntu Server 22.04 in ap-south-1. The same Ubuntu image in us-east-1 has a completely different AMI ID.

terms.definition: An AWS CLI command that stores your AWS credentials (Access Key ID, Secret Access Key), default region, and output format locally for use by the CLI and SDK.
terms.example: Running aws configure saves credentials to ~/.aws/credentials. Boto3 scripts then automatically use those credentials without any code changes.

terms.definition: An S3 feature that allows a bucket to serve HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files directly as a website via a public endpoint URL.
terms.example: Enable Static Website Hosting on an S3 bucket, set index.html as the index document, and S3 provides a URL to access the site.
